subtitle: When Songs Crowned One King and Memory Crowned Another

panels.shot: split-frame wide, half showing a shining court poet beside Yashovarman in Kannauj, half a misty mountain hall with Lalitaditya looming over a bowed captive king
panels.action: On one side, Yashovarman of Kannauj sits crowned on a terrace as a blind poet declaims before him; on the other, Lalitaditya of Kashmir stands in a high mountain hall, a captive king kneeling at his feet, snow peaks beyond.

dialogue.text: In one age, a poet made Yashovarman the master of the north; four centuries later, a Kashmiri chronicler swore Lalitaditya broke that very king. Which memory do we believe?

i18n.hi: एक युग में कवि ने यशोवर्मन को उत्तर का स्वामी बनाया; चार सौ बरस बाद कश्मीरी इतिहासकार ने कसम खाई कि ललितादित्य ने उसी राजा को तोड़ दिया। किस याद पर भरोसा करें?

panels.shot: slow push-in over a map-like vista of north India, rivers and cities picked out in dawn light
panels.action: A wide view of the upper Gangetic plain and the mountains to the north, rivers curling like silver; the Ganga valley around Kannauj lies flat and fertile, while Kashmir is a green bowl ringed with snow, both marked by small palace silhouettes.

dialogue.text: After Harsha’s death, the north had no single master. Kannauj glittered at the heart of the plains, while in the mountain bowl of Kashmir, the Karkotas were quietly forging their own crown.

i18n.hi: हर्ष के बाद उत्तर में कोई एक मालिक न रहा। मैदानों के दिल में कन्नौज जगमगाता था, और पहाड़ों की कटोरी कश्मीर में कार्कोटा चुपचाप अपना मुकुट गढ़ रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Yashovarman’s court, low angle to emphasize majesty
panels.action: Yashovarman sits on a carved throne beneath punkha fans in a busy Kannauj hall, courtiers ranked around him; beside him stands the blind poet Vakpati, head tilted, fingers hovering in the air as if tracing words.

dialogue.text: In Kannauj, Yashovarman rose from Harsha’s shadow, gathering feudatories, pushing his banner toward Gauda. His poet Vakpati, blind but sharp, called him the slayer of Gauda—the Gaudavaho.

i18n.hi: कन्नौज में हर्ष की परछाईं से यशोवर्मन उभरा, सामंत जोड़े, अपना ध्वज गाढ़ा की तरफ बढ़ाया। उसका कवि वाक्पति, नेत्रहीन पर तेज, उसे गौड़-वध करने वाला—गौड़वहो—गाता रहा।

panels.shot: tight three-quarter view of Vakpati performing, with Yashovarman listening, torchlight flickering
panels.action: Vakpati stands with one hand lifted in a sweeping gesture, mouth open mid-chant; Yashovarman leans forward, intent and pleased, as courtiers listen in rapt silence in the torchlit hall.

dialogue.speaker: yashovarman_of_kannauj_and_lalitaditya_of_kashmi
dialogue.text: Sing it again, Vakpati. Let the world hear how Gauda fell.

i18n.hi: फिर गा, वाक्पति। दुनिया सुने कैसे गौड़ गिरा।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye of a marching army on the plains, stretching toward the horizon
panels.action: Columns of Yashovarman’s troops move across the dusty plain, banners snapping, elephants lumbering, horsemen riding along the flanks; in the distance, a walled city suggests Gauda’s land.

dialogue.text: The poem roared of marches eastward, of Gauda humbled, of kings who once bowed only to Harsha now sending their obedience to Kannauj. The Ganga plains buzzed with this new claimant to greatness.

i18n.hi: कविता गूँजी पूरब की चढ़ाइयों से, झुके हुए गौड़ से, उन राजाओं से जो कभी बस हर्ष को झुकते थे, अब अपनी आज्ञाकारिता कन्नौज भेजते थे। गंगा के मैदानी इलाकों में नए दावेदार की सरगर्मी थी।

panels.shot: medium shot, low angle, Lalitaditya in a Kashmiri council hall with mountains visible through arches
panels.action: In a stone-pillared hall in Kashmir, Lalitaditya stands over a floor map, hand resting on his sword hilt, ministers gathered around; beyond the arches, a serene lake reflects snow-clad peaks.

dialogue.text: Far to the north, Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkotas ruled a very different realm: a valley like a fortress, a court that watched Silk Road caravans, and a king hungry to ride beyond the passes.

i18n.hi: दूर उत्तर में कार्कोटा वंश का ललितादित्य मुक्तापीड बिल्कुल अलग राज चलाता था: किले-सी घाटी, रेशम मार्ग की रखवाली करती अटकती निगाहें, और एक राजा जो दर्रों के पार घोड़ा दौड़ाने को भूखा था।

panels.shot: close-up on a Chinese monk-scholar at a writing desk, with faint ghost-images of foreign kings behind him
panels.action: A robed East Asian monk, Huichao, sits cross-legged with a brush over a scroll, eyes thoughtful; behind him, translucent silhouettes of Indian kings and Central Asian envoys suggest the distant realms he describes.

dialogue.text: Travelers like Huichao and Chinese annals spoke of Kashmir and its neighbors as players in a wider game, where Indian kings dealt with Turks and Tang envoys. In that world, Lalitaditya’s name rose often.

i18n.hi: हुईचाओ जैसे यात्री और चीनी लिखतें बताते हैं कि कश्मीर और उसके पड़ोसी बड़े खेल के खिलाड़ी थे, जहाँ भारतीय राजा तुर्कों और तांग दूतों से सौदा करते थे। उस दुनिया में ललितादित्य का नाम बार-बार उठता है।

panels.shot: dramatic split-diagonal, Kannauj court on one side, Kashmir court on the other, both looking outward
panels.action: On one half, Yashovarman and his courtiers stand on a palace balcony over the Ganga, pointing east and west; on the other, Lalitaditya stands at a high window above the Jhelum, gazing south and beyond the passes.

dialogue.text: Two courts, two centers of ambition. Kannauj claimed the plains, Kashmir the highlands and roads beyond. Neither could ignore the other forever. But our sources do not tell us exactly when their paths crossed.

i18n.hi: दो दरबार, दो महत्वाकांक्षा के कें द्र। मैदानों पर दावा कन्नौज का, पहाड़ों और राहों पर कश्मीर का। वे हमेशा एक-दूसरे को नहीं टाल सकते थे। पर हमारे स्रोत नहीं बताते कि उनकी राहें कब सचमुच टकराईं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Kalhana in his study, scrolls around, with faint imagined battle scenes behind him
panels.action: In twelfth-century Kashmir, Kalhana sits amid piles of palm-leaf manuscripts, head bent over his writing; ghostly scenes of marching troops and kneeling kings hover in the smoky background, shaped by his words.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Kalhana in his Rajatarangini reached back to that seventh and eighth century struggle. Sifting older tales and records, he painted Lalitaditya as a conqueror beyond measure.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद कल्हण ने अपनी राजतरंगिणी में सातवीं-आठवीं सदी के उस टकराव को टटोला। पुरानी कथाएँ और लेखाहिसाब छानकर उसने ललितादित्य को असीम विजेता बना खींचा।

panels.shot: wide shot, stylized, Lalitaditya’s army descending from a Himalayan pass toward hazy plains
panels.action: Lalitaditya rides at the head of armoured horsemen descending a steep mountain pass, mists curling around them; below lies a hazy suggestion of the plains, a river glinting faintly in the distance.

dialogue.text: Kalhana’s Lalitaditya rides through deserts and passes, subduing foes from the northwest to the plains. He names many lands, and among the kings the Kashmiri lion humbles, he places Yashovarman of Kannauj.

i18n.hi: कल्हण का ललितादित्य रेगिस्तानों और दर्रों से होकर दौड़ता है, उत्तर-पश्चिम से लेकर मैदानों तक दुश्मनों को झुकाता है। वह कई देशों के नाम गिनता है, और जिन राजाओं को यह कश्मीरी सिंह नीचा दिखाता है, उनमें वह कन्नौज के यशोवर्मन को भी रखता है।

panels.shot: medium shot, indistinct battlefield plain under overcast sky, armies facing off, no gore
panels.action: Two massed armies face each other across a dusty plain under a brooding sky, banners of Kashmir and Kannauj visible but details blurred, as if seen through the haze of memory; both kings are specks amid the ranks.

dialogue.text: We do not know on which field they met, how many marched, or how the lines were drawn. Kalhana describes victory, not logistics. The historian must hold back where his sources fall silent.

i18n.hi: हम नहीं जानते किस मैदान पर मुलाकात हुई, कितने चले, कहाँ पंक्तियाँ खिंचीं। कल्हण जीत बताता है, रसद नहीं। इतिहासकार को वहीं रुकना पड़ता है जहाँ उसके स्रोत चुप हो जाते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Lalitaditya under a cloudy sky, with a distant king’s standard lowered in the background
panels.action: Lalitaditya sits firm astride his horse, face stern yet calm, as in the far background a royal standard bearing a symbol of Kannauj tilts downward amid defeated troops dispersing.

dialogue.text: Yet through the haze, a shape emerges. In Kalhana’s telling, Lalitaditya breaks Yashovarman’s pride. His chronicle speaks of the king of Kannauj as a rival checked, his freedom bent to the Kashmiri will.

i18n.hi: फिर भी धुंध में एक आकृति बनती है। कल्हण के लेखे में ललितादित्य यशोवर्मन का घमंड तोड़ता है। उसकी कथा कन्नौज के राजा को रोके हुए प्रतिद्वंद्वी के रूप में गाती है, जिसकी आज़ादी अब कश्मीरी इच्छा के आगे झुकी है।

panels.shot: dramatic interior of a mountain palace hall, low angle on Lalitaditya with a kneeling, shackled royal figure
panels.action: In a grand hall with carved stone columns and open windows onto mountain slopes, Lalitaditya stands on a dais, while before him a richly dressed but shackled king kneels, head bowed, hands loosely bound; attendants watch from the shadows.

dialogue.text: Kalhana even conjures a captive king of the plains, brought to the Kashmiri court in chains. Many see in this humbled ruler Yashovarman himself, though the text, like the hall, is filled with echoes, not certainties.

i18n.hi: कल्हण तो मैदानों के एक बंदी राजा को भी बुला लेता है, जंजीरों में जकड़ा, कश्मीरी दरबार में लाया गया। कई लोग इस झुके शासक में खुद यशोवर्मन को देखते हैं, हालांकि ग्रंथ भी, सभा की तरह, गूँजों से भरे हैं, यकीन से नहीं।

panels.shot: tight shot on a kneeling king’s profile, face partly in shadow, no explicit name, Lalitaditya blurred in background
panels.action: The profile of the kneeling king fills the frame, jaw clenched, eyes downcast yet burning; behind him, slightly out of focus, Lalitaditya watches with an unreadable expression, one hand raised in a gesture of command.

dialogue.speaker: yashovarman_of_kannauj_and_lalitaditya_of_kashmi
dialogue.text: So this is how songs end—before another man’s throne.

i18n.hi: गीत ऐसे ही खत्म होते हैं—किसी और की गद्दी के आगे।

panels.shot: intercut close-ups: Vakpati reciting, Kalhana writing, their faces mirrored
panels.action: On one side, Vakpati’s aged, blind face is lifted in recitation; on the other, Kalhana’s younger, sighted face bends over a palm-leaf, stylus scratching; their profiles mirror each other in a dark background.

dialogue.text: But in the Gaudavaho, there is no defeat, no chain, no Lalitaditya. Vakpati’s poem ends with Yashovarman triumphant. The Kashmiri chronicle remembers what the Kannauj court song chose to forget.

i18n.hi: पर गौड़वहो में न हार है, न जंजीर, न ललितादित्य। वाक्पति की कविता यशोवर्मन को विजयी पर छोड़ती है। कश्मीरी इतिहास वही याद करता है जिसे कन्नौज का दरबारी गीत भूल जाना चाहता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Yashovarman older, in a quieter court, some seats empty, a map of the north behind him
panels.action: An older Yashovarman sits on his throne in a dimmer hall, fewer courtiers present; behind him, a painted panel-map of north India shows Kannauj smaller, other polities more prominent than before.

dialogue.text: We glimpse Yashovarman’s later years only in fragments. His moment as the unchallenged voice of the north did not last. Other powers stirred, and in memory, Kannauj’s brief blaze faded faster than Kashmir’s legend.

i18n.hi: यशोवर्मन के आख़िरी सालों की झलक हमें सिर्फ टुकड़ों में मिलती है। उत्तर की अकेली आवाज़ के रूप में उसका पल टिक नहीं पाया। दूसरी शक्तियाँ उठीं, और याद में कन्नौज की चमक कश्मीर की कथा से जल्दी मद्धम पड़ गई।

panels.shot: grand wide shot of Lalitaditya’s imagined empire, then parts of it fading like mist
panels.action: A sweeping vista shows Lalitaditya standing atop a hill, lands and cities stretching out in all directions; as the image progresses, some distant cities and banners blur and dissolve like mist, leaving a smaller yet still impressive realm clear.

dialogue.text: Kalhana’s Lalitaditya strides across Iran, Central Asia, the whole of India. Modern historians pull that world-conquest back to earth, keeping what later records and foreign notices can support, letting the rest drift away as courtly mist.

i18n.hi: कल्हण का ललितादित्य ईरान, मध्य एशिया, पूरे भारत पर छाया फैलाता है। आधुनिक इतिहासकार उस विश्व-विजय को ज़मीन पर उतारते हैं, वहीं तक रखते हैं जिसे बाद के पुराने लेख और विदेशी गवाहियाँ सहारा दें, बाकी को दरबारी धुंध होने देते हैं।

panels.shot: intimate shot of a scholar’s hands laying Gaudavaho and Rajatarangini side by side on a table
panels.action: At a wooden desk lit by an oil lamp, a modern scholar’s hands place two old manuscripts side by side: one labeled in script as Gaudavaho, the other as Rajatarangini; marginal notes and a small map of north India lie nearby.

dialogue.text: Between Vakpati and Kalhana, between poem and chronicle, we piece together a quieter story: two great kings in one generation, their rivalry real, their clash remembered unevenly, their empires more modest than either praise-song admits.

i18n.hi: वाक्पति और कल्हण के बीच, कविता और इतिहास के बीच, हम एक शांत कहानी जोड़ते हैं: एक ही पीढ़ी के दो बड़े राजा, जिनकी प्रतिद्वंद्विता सच्ची, पर टक्कर की याद टेढ़ी-मेढ़ी, और जिनके साम्राज्य उतने भी बड़े नहीं जितने उनके गुणगान दावा करते हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot, ghostly silhouettes of both kings behind a present-day historian and a listening crowd
panels.action: In a modern lecture hall or museum gallery, a historian gestures toward a display of maps and inscriptions as a diverse audience listens; behind them, faint towering silhouettes of Yashovarman and Lalitaditya loom, made of script and fading lines.

dialogue.text: Yashovarman’s glory-song and Lalitaditya’s chronicle-empire remind us that power writes in different inks. To know the past, we must read against the grain of praise, and let silence weigh as heavily as boast.

i18n.hi: यशोवर्मन के विजय-गीत और ललितादित्य के इतिहास-सम्राज्य याद दिलाते हैं कि सत्ता अलग-अलग स्याही से लिखती है। अतीत को सच में जानने के लिए हमें प्रशंसा के खिलाफ पढ़ना होगा, और चुप्पी को भी उतना ही भारी मानना होगा जितना शेखी को।

title_i18n.en: The Blind Poet and the Captive King

subtitle_i18n.en: When Songs Crowned One King and Memory Crowned Another
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब गीतों ने एक को, यादों ने दूसरे को ताज पहनाया
